summary: Map the 6 Ops/setup commands (completion/doctor/onboard/permissions/setup/list-symbols-html) for Phase 4 of the remctl Swift port

findings.area: completion + setup commands (cmd_completion, cmd_setup, completion-script generation, config-dir/0700 creation) for Phase 4 of the remctl Python to Swift port
findings.summary: cmd_completion (remctl:7309) and cmd_setup (remctl:7516) are pure filesystem/string commands with NO SQL and NO DB dependency. `completion <shell>` writes one of three hand-written, hardcoded multi-line string constants (ZSH_COMPLETION :6410, BASH_COMPLETION :6710, FISH_COMPLETION :6784) to stdout, selected by get_completion_script (:6951). `setup` creates CONFIG_DIR (default ~/.config/remctl) with mkdir(parents=True) + chmod(0o700) (best-effort, OSError swallowed), resolves a shell, installs the same completion script to a fixed per-shell target path, prints a human or JSON summary, and (with --doctor) optionally appends doctor output. The Swift port already has the matching config-dir resolver (Paths.resolveConfigDir, Paths.swift:24) and the same 3 official subcommand lists embedded in argument-parser command structs. KEY DECISION on completion-script generation: I recommend a HYBRID — keep `completion <shell>` porting the hand-written scripts verbatim (string constants) for byte-for-byte contract parity, and do NOT switch to ArgumentParser's built-in generator. Rationale below.
keyFindings: cmd_completion (:7309): `shell = a.shell if present else 'zsh'`; `sys.stdout.write(get_completion_script(shell))` (no trailing newline beyond what the script literal already contains). On ValueError prints to STDERR `Error: <exc>. Use bash, zsh, or fish.` and sys.exit(1). NOTE: full message would be e.g. `Error: Unsupported shell 'xyz'. Use bash, zsh, or fish.` But argparse choices=[bash,zsh,fish] (subparser registered at :8114, positional `shell` nargs='?' default='zsh') reject bad values with exit 2 BEFORE the handler, so the ValueError branch is practically unreachable. completion has NO --json flag; --format json is ignored (raw script still emitted).
get_completion_script(shell) (:6951): returns ZSH_COMPLETION / BASH_COMPLETION / FISH_COMPLETION; else raise ValueError(f"Unsupported shell '{shell}'").

The three scripts are LITERAL hand-maintained strings (not generated). ZSH (:6410-6708): `#compdef remctl`, `_remctl()` with `local -a commands=(...)` of 47 'name:desc' entries in source order, a `case "$words[2]" in` block with per-command `_arguments` specs (show/templates/template-info/add/edit/doctor/link/export/list-symbols/smart-list-create/smart-list-edit/smart-list-delete/template-create/template-apply/template-delete/list-create/list-edit/list-rename/list-pin|list-unpin/list-delete), ends `_describe 'command' commands`, `}`, `compdef _remctl remctl`. BASH (:6710-6782): `_remctl() {` with `commands="lists smart-lists ... completion"` (space-separated, 45 names), an if/elif chain on `${COMP_WORDS[1]}` using `compgen -W`, ends `complete -F _remctl remctl`. FISH (:6784-6949): `# Fish completion for remctl` then `complete -c remctl -n "__fish_use_subcommand" -a <cmd> -d "<desc>"` lines + `__fish_seen_subcommand_from` flag lines.

The bash/fish scripts contain extra flags absent from zsh: e.g. bash smart-list-create/edit include `--date-today-include-past-due` (zsh does not). The three scripts are NOT perfectly consistent with each other — faithful porting means reproducing each verbatim, including these inconsistencies.

cmd_setup (:7516): (1) CONFIG_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); (2) try CONFIG_DIR.chmod(0o700) except OSError pass; (3) selected_shell = resolve_setup_shell(a.shell); (4) if != 'skip', completion_path = install_completion(selected_shell) inside try/except ValueError (prints `Error: <exc>` to stderr, sys.exit(1)); (5) build result dict; (6) optional doctor block; (7) print JSON or human.

resolve_setup_shell(requested) (:6983): if requested != 'auto' return it verbatim (INCLUDING 'skip' and 'bash'/'zsh'/'fish'); else detect_shell_name() and return it only if in {zsh,bash,fish} else 'skip'.
detect_shell_name() (:6961): basename of $SHELL env, or 'zsh' if $SHELL unset/empty. (Path(shell).name)

completion_target_path(shell) (:6966): zsh -> ~/.zsh/completions/_remctl ; bash -> ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/remctl ; fish -> ~/.config/fish/completions/remctl.fish ; else ValueError. NOTE these are NOT under CONFIG_DIR and do NOT honor XDG (the fish path is a literal ~/.config, not $XDG_CONFIG_HOME).

install_completion(shell) (:6976): target=completion_target_path(shell); target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); target.write_text(get_completion_script(shell)); return target. Overwrites unconditionally; NO 0600 chmod on the completion file (unlike write_private_text_file).

CONFIG_DIR = resolve_config_dir('remctl') (remctl:54). resolve_config_dir (remctl_runtime.py:33): REMCTL_CONFIG_DIR (expanduser, used AS-IS no appName append) > XDG_CONFIG_HOME/appName > ~/.config/appName. Swift Paths.resolveConfigDir (Paths.swift:24) already replicates this EXACTLY including the no-append REMCTL_CONFIG_DIR branch.

--doctor sub-option (:7537): if a.doctor, result['doctor'] = {'ok': <no fails>, 'checks': gather_doctor_checks()} — a SMALLER shape than top-level `doctor --json` (no warnings/failures/context keys). In human mode (:7558) it ALSO calls cmd_doctor(SimpleNamespace(json=False)) which RE-RUNS doctor and can itself sys.exit(1) on any fail — so human setup --doctor can exit non-zero; JSON setup --doctor never does (only gather_doctor_checks runs, no exit).

Swift stubs: CompletionCmd (OpsCommands.swift:196, named to avoid AP's own Completion) and Setup (:220) both `throw NotImplemented(...)`. IMPORTANT MISMATCH: CompletionCmd currently has only `@OptionGroup var output: JSONOptions` and NO positional `shell` argument; Python's completion takes a positional `shell` (choices bash/zsh/fish, default zsh) and has NO --json. Setup currently only has JSONOptions and lacks `--shell` (choices auto/bash/zsh/fish/skip, default auto) and `--doctor`. Both stubs need their argument surface corrected during Phase 4.

The doctor `completion` check (gather_doctor_checks :7414-7424) reuses detect_shell_name + completion_target_path: detail `<shell>: <path>` (ok iff path exists), warn fix `Run remctl setup --shell <shell> to install completion.`; for non-{zsh,bash,fish} shell -> warn, detail `Unsupported shell '<shell>'`, fix `Run remctl setup --shell zsh|bash|fish.`. config_dir check (:7406): ok/warn on CONFIG_DIR.exists(), warn fix `Run remctl setup to create config files.`

findings.ciTestability: "HIGHLY CI-testable (no GUI, no TCC, no DB). PURE/string: get_completion_script (assert exact bytes per shell), resolve_setup_shell (env-driven), detect_shell_name (env-driven), completion_target_path (fixed strings). Filesystem (CI-testable with REMCTL_CONFIG_DIR/HOME override to a temp dir): cmd_setup config-dir creation + 0700 chmod + completion install + human/JSON output. Contract already lists golden tests: resolve_setup_shell('auto') with SHELL=/bin/tcsh->'skip', /bin/zsh->'zsh' (line 2762); cmd_setup(shell='skip',doctor=False,json=False) stdout contains 'RemCTL setup','Shell completion: skipped','remctl onboard' (2763); resolve_config_dir precedence (2787). The chmod(0700) is best-effort and may be unobservable on some CI filesystems — assert it does not throw, optionally assert st_mode when on a POSIX fs. The ONLY environment-dependent corner is setup --doctor (pulls in doctor's fs/process probes), but setup --doctor + JSON never exits and is testable with env overrides; setup --doctor + HUMAN re-runs doctor and may sys.exit on a real machine — test the no-doctor and JSON-doctor paths in CI, leave human-doctor short-circuit to integration."
findings.outwardFacing: "setup WRITES the filesystem: creates CONFIG_DIR (default ~/.config/remctl, mode 0700) and writes a completion script to a fixed per-shell target under $HOME (~/.zsh/completions/_remctl, ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/remctl, or ~/.config/fish/completions/remctl.fish), creating parent dirs and OVERWRITING any existing file. These are user-facing, mildly hard-to-reverse (it drops files in the user's shell config tree), but low-risk and idempotent. It does NOT launch any GUI, prompt TCC, touch the Reminders DB, run EventKit/AppleScript, or require Full Disk Access. completion is fully read-only (writes only to stdout). Both are in AUTO_ONBOARD_SKIP_COMMANDS so they never trigger first-launch onboarding. For Swift parity, all writes MUST be redirectable via REMCTL_CONFIG_DIR / HOME so CI never pollutes a real home dir."
findings.implementationApproach: "RECOMMENDATION: HYBRID — port the hand-written scripts VERBATIM for the `completion` command; do NOT use ArgumentParser's built-in generator for it. Concretely: (a) For `completion`: add the three script literals as Swift static string constants (e.g. CompletionScripts.zsh/.bash/.fish) copied byte-for-byte from remctl:6410/6710/6784, and have CompletionCmd take a positional `shell` (ExpressibleByArgument enum bash/zsh/fish, default zsh, NO --json) and write the chosen literal to stdout. This guarantees byte-identical output the contract pins (line 1037-1040) and keeps the 3 install target paths correct. (b) FIX the Swift arg surface: CompletionCmd currently lacks the positional `shell` and wrongly carries JSONOptions — replace with `@Argument var shell: ShellChoice = .zsh`; Setup currently lacks `--shell`(auto/bash/zsh/fish/skip default auto) and `--doctor` — add both plus keep --json. (c) For `setup`: port resolve_setup_shell/detect_shell_name/completion_target_path/install_completion as small pure Swift helpers; reuse existing Paths.resolveConfigDir; mkdir CONFIG_DIR + best-effort chmod(0o700) via FileManager.setAttributes wrapped so failures are ignored (matches OSError-swallow, contract line 1853); write the completion literal via install; emit the exact human/JSON shapes above (JSON via the existing OrderedJSON/printJSON path with indent=2 to preserve key order ok/config_dir/completion_shell/completion_path[/doctor]). For setup --doctor, gate on Phase-4 doctor being ported; replicate the human-mode short-circuit only if doctor's exit semantics are reproduced, else emit the JSON-embedded checks shape. TRADEOFFS of verbatim vs AP-builtin: VERBATIM PROS = exact contract/golden-test parity, identical install paths, no behavior drift, lets the same scripts ship regardless of how Swift parses args; CONS = double maintenance (the literals must be updated by hand when flags change, same burden Python already carries — acceptable since this is a faithful port, not a redesign). AP-BUILTIN PROS = auto-derives completions from the command tree, zero hand maintenance; CONS = produces DIFFERENT script text/structure (fails byte-parity tests at contract line 1037-1040), emits to AP's own conventions/paths, requires the full command tree + help strings to already match Python exactly to even approximate parity, and AP's zsh/bash/fish output differs from these hand-tuned `_arguments`/`compgen`/`complete` forms. Since the mandate is a faithful port with a pinned contract, verbatim wins. (Optional future: expose AP's `--generate-completion-script` as an UNDOCUMENTED extra, but keep `completion <shell>` verbatim as the contract surface.)"
risks: Swift arg-surface mismatch: CompletionCmd (OpsCommands.swift:196) is missing the positional `shell` and wrongly has JSONOptions; Setup (:220) is missing `--shell` and `--doctor`. If Phase 4 ports behavior without fixing these signatures, `remctl completion bash` and `remctl setup --shell zsh --doctor` will fail to parse — must update structs.

Byte-parity hazard: if Phase 4 chooses AP's built-in generator, the contract's pinned script structure (spec lines 1037-1040: 47/45 command counts, exact start/end markers) will NOT match and golden tests break. Verbatim porting avoids this but requires copying the literals EXACTLY (including the bash/fish-only `--date-today-include-past-due` flag and other cross-shell inconsistencies, and the trailing newline inside each triple-quoted constant).
The three Python scripts are internally INCONSISTENT (zsh omits flags that bash/fish include). A 'helpful' Swift dev might 'fix' them — do NOT; faithful parity means reproducing the inconsistencies.

setup --doctor coupling: human-mode re-invokes cmd_doctor and can sys.exit(1) mid-setup; JSON-mode embeds a DIFFERENT smaller doctor shape and never exits. Swift must replicate both branches distinctly AND depends on Phase-4 doctor being ported first (the doctor `bridge`/`private_helper`/`permissions_helper` checks themselves need re-framing for the in-process reality per the task brief).

chmod(0o700) is best-effort (OSError swallowed, contract 1853). Swift's FileManager.setAttributes throwing must be caught-and-ignored, and on some CI filesystems the resulting mode is unobservable — tests should assert no-throw rather than exact mode there.

Filesystem write side effects: completion install paths are fixed under $HOME and NOT under CONFIG_DIR/XDG (fish target is literal ~/.config, not $XDG_CONFIG_HOME). CI must override HOME (and REMCTL_CONFIG_DIR for the config dir) to avoid polluting a real home; the fish target specifically will ignore XDG so HOME override is required.

completion's unreachable-but-specified error message `Error: <exc>. Use bash, zsh, or fish.` (note the embedded ValueError text `Unsupported shell '<shell>'`) should be preserved for parity even though AP/argparse choices make it unreachable — Swift's ExpressibleByArgument enum will similarly reject bad values before run().

findings.area: doctor (cmd_doctor / gather_doctor_checks) — Phase 4 recon, Python source-of-truth
findings.summary: `cmd_doctor` is a pure-ish reporter: it calls `gather_doctor_checks()` (builds an ordered list of 11 check dicts `{name,status,detail,fix}`), `doctor_execution_context()` (process-ancestry / host-app introspection), computes `fail_count`/`warn_count`, assembles a `result` dict, optionally prints JSON (`--json`) or a human report (`print_check_report`), and exits 1 iff any check FAILED (warnings never fail). The 11 checks in order are: platform, python, store_dir, database, cli, bridge, private_helper, permissions_helper, config_dir, completion. (database has two mutually-exclusive code paths.) THREE checks — `bridge`, `private_helper`, `permissions_helper` — probe for EXTERNAL helper binaries (remctl-bridge/remctl-private/remctl-permissions) that no longer exist in the Swift in-process port and MUST be re-framed. The `python` check and the Python-interpreter clipboard/FDA-target language are also Python-runtime artifacts that change meaning when the runtime is a compiled Swift binary. The check-gathering is highly CI-testable if STORE_DIR/CONFIG_DIR/exe-path/auth-status are injectable; the host-app/terminal detection and FDA-helper launching are environment/GUI-dependent.
keyFindings: gather_doctor_checks (remctl:7320) builds checks via local `add(name,status,detail,fix)` appending {"name","status","detail","fix"}. Order is fixed: platform, python, store_dir, database, cli, bridge, private_helper, permissions_helper, config_dir, completion (10 add() calls; database path is single but two-branched; completion is single but two-branched). Total = 10 checks normally.

CHECK 1 platform: ok iff sys.platform=='darwin' else FAIL. detail = `f"{platform.system()} {platform.mac_ver()[0] or platform.release()}"` (e.g. 'Darwin 25.5.0'). fix(on fail)='RemCTL only supports macOS.'

CHECK 2 python: ok iff sys.version_info>=(3,10) else FAIL. detail=platform.python_version() (e.g. '3.11.6'). fix='Install Python 3.10 or newer.' — THIS CHECK IS A PYTHON-RUNTIME ARTIFACT; in Swift there is no interpreter version to gate. Re-frame to a Swift/OS-version or runtime check, or drop.

CHECK 3 store_dir: ok iff STORE_DIR.exists() else FAIL. detail=str(STORE_DIR). fix='Set REMCTL_STORE_DIR if your Reminders store lives elsewhere.' STORE_DIR=resolve_store_dir() = $REMCTL_STORE_DIR or ~/Library/Group Containers/group.com.apple.reminders/Container_v1/Stores. Swift equivalent: Paths.resolveStoreDir() already exists (Paths.swift:16).

CHECK 4 database: TWO branches. If reminders_store_access_error() returns a non-None string (store dir exists but NOT os.R_OK readable → FDA blocked): status=FAIL, detail=that error string, fix=full_disk_access_fix_text(rerun_command='remctl doctor --for-agent', mention_onboard=True). ELSE: db_path=find_main_db_path(); status='ok' if db_path else 'FAIL'; detail=str(db_path) or 'No Reminders database found'; fix(on fail)='Enable iCloud Reminders and open Reminders.app once, or run remctl onboard.' Swift has Paths.storeAccessError() and Paths.findMainDBPath() already (Paths.swift:36,49) — DIRECT PORT.

CHECK 5 cli: ok iff current_cli_path().exists() else FAIL. detail=str(cli_path). fix=None if shutil.which('remctl') is not None else f'Add {cli_path.parent} to PATH.' NOTE the ok/fail status keys off cli_path.exists() but the FIX keys off cli_on_path (PATH presence) — so a present-but-not-on-PATH binary shows OK with a fix string. current_cli_path()=shutil.which('remctl') resolved, else Path(__file__).resolve(). Swift: use CommandLine.arguments[0]/Bundle.main.executablePath + a which('remctl') lookup.

CHECK 6 bridge: EXTERNAL-BINARY CHECK — RE-FRAME. ok iff bridge_path.exists() and os.access(X_OK) else WARN (never fail). detail=str(bridge_path). fix(on not-ok)='Run ./install.sh or compile remctl-bridge.swift with swiftc, then run remctl onboard.' bridge_path=current_bridge_path(). In the Swift port EventKit is in-process, so probe EKEventStore authorization instead of a binary.

CHECK 7 private_helper: EXTERNAL-BINARY CHECK — RE-FRAME. ok iff private_path.exists() and X_OK else WARN. detail=str(private_path). fix='Run ./install.sh to compile remctl-private, or avoid --private writes.' private_path=current_private_path(). In Swift, ReminderKit is linked in-process — probe via RKPProbe() (returns 'reminderkit-ok'/'reminderkit-missing', ReminderKitPrivate.m:205).

CHECK 8 permissions_helper: EXTERNAL-BINARY CHECK — RE-FRAME/likely DROP. ok iff permissions_path.exists() and X_OK else WARN. detail=str(permissions_path). fix='Run ./install.sh to compile remctl-permissions for the guided Full Disk Access flow.' permissions_path=current_permissions_path(). The guided GUI helper is the most environment-coupled; in-process there is no separate permissions binary.

CHECK 9 config_dir: ok iff CONFIG_DIR.exists() else WARN. detail=str(CONFIG_DIR). fix='Run remctl setup to create config files.' CONFIG_DIR=resolve_config_dir('remctl') = $REMCTL_CONFIG_DIR | $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/remctl | ~/.config/remctl. Swift: Paths.resolveConfigDir() exists (Paths.swift:24).

CHECK 10 completion: TWO branches. shell=detect_shell_name(). If shell in {zsh,bash,fish}: completion_path=completion_target_path(shell); status='ok' if exists else WARN; detail=f'{shell}: {completion_path}'; fix(on missing)=f'Run remctl setup --shell {shell} to install completion.' ELSE (unsupported shell): status=WARN, detail=f"Unsupported shell '{shell}'", fix='Run remctl setup --shell zsh|bash|fish.'

EXIT CODE: cmd_doctor exits 1 iff fail_count>0 (`if fail_count: sys.exit(1)`). WARN never causes nonzero exit. So with the three helper checks downgraded to WARN, only platform/python/store_dir/database/cli failures produce exit 1.

--for-agent (argparse: c.add_argument('--for-agent', action='store_true'), remctl:8062) does TWO things: (a) JSON path adds result['agent_note'] (3-sentence string about process-context scoping of FDA). (b) human path prints an 'Agent note:' line after the context block. It does NOT change any check status. It IS passed into the database-check fix text indirectly only via the hard-coded rerun_command='remctl doctor --for-agent'.

doctor_execution_context() (remctl:3270) returns {python: sys.executable, pid: os.getpid(), parent_process: ancestry[0] or None, terminal_app, host_app, effective_context}. It walks process_ancestry() (ps -o ppid/ucomm/command up the tree, limit 8), uses detect_terminal_app_name() (TERM_PROGRAM env + ps walk against KNOWN_TERMINAL_APPS), and _app_name_from_process_name() (special-cases 'codex'→'Codex.app'). effective_context = 'Terminal' | 'Codex' | <AppName w/o .app> | 'unknown'.

doctor is read-only / SAFE: it only reads paths, env, runs `ps`/`mdfind` for context, and prints. It does NOT modify the system, launch GUI, or prompt TCC. (The TCC-prompting & GUI-launch live in onboard/permissions, not doctor.)
findings.helpers:
Direct helpers cmd_doctor/gather_doctor_checks call, with signatures and behavior:

- reminders_store_access_error() -> str|None (remctl:171): returns FDA-blocked message ONLY if `STORE_DIR.exists() and not os.access(STORE_DIR, os.R_OK)`, else None. Message text: 'Direct CLI reads are blocked because the Reminders store at {STORE_DIR} is not readable from this process context ({sys.executable}). This usually means Full Disk Access is missing for the app or interpreter that is running remctl here.' SWIFT EXISTS: Paths.storeAccessError(storeDir:) (Paths.swift:49) — byte-identical message, uses Bundle.main.executablePath instead of sys.executable.

- find_main_db_path() -> Path|None (remctl:191): returns None if reminders_store_access_error() truthy; else globs STORE_DIR/'Data-*.sqlite' sorted by st_size descending, returns largest or None. SWIFT EXISTS: Paths.findMainDBPath(storeDir:) (Paths.swift:36) — same largest-by-size logic (does NOT pre-gate on access error, but the database check branches before calling it, so behavior matches).

- current_cli_path() -> Path (remctl:6990): shutil.which('remctl') resolved, else Path(__file__).resolve().
- current_bridge_path() -> Path (remctl:7001): $REMCTL_BRIDGE_PATH expanded, else BRIDGE_PATH if exists (resolved), else which('remctl-bridge'), else BRIDGE_PATH.resolve(). BRIDGE_PATH=resolve_binary_path(__file__,'remctl-bridge','REMCTL_BRIDGE_PATH').
- current_private_path() -> Path (remctl:7013): same shape for remctl-private / $REMCTL_PRIVATE_PATH.
- current_permissions_path() -> Path (remctl:7025): same shape for remctl-permissions / $REMCTL_PERMISSIONS_PATH.
  (resolve_binary_path, remctl_runtime.py:66: $env override, else first existing of [scriptdir/name, scriptdir/bin/name, ~/bin/name, ~/.local/bin/name], else which(name), else scriptdir/name.)

- doctor_execution_context() -> dict (remctl:3270): see keyFindings. Calls process_ancestry(limit=8) (remctl:3247 → process_info via `ps -p PID -o ppid= -o ucomm= -o command=`), detect_terminal_app_name() (remctl:3183: TERM_PROGRAM normalized then 6-level ps walk on comm against KNOWN_TERMINAL_APPS dict), _app_name_from_process_name() (remctl:3261: 'codex'→'Codex.app' else _normalize_terminal_app_name).

- print_check_report(title, checks) -> (warn_count, fail_count) (remctl:3149): if title prints bold title; for each check prints `[<COLOR-LABEL>] {name}: {detail}` where label OK=green/WARN=yellow/FAIL=red; if check['fix'], prints each fix line indented 6 spaces dim. Then a summary line: `{N} checks, {w} warning(s), {f} failure(s)` colored red if any fail, else yellow if any warn, else green. doctor calls it as print_check_report(None, checks) (no title — doctor prints its own 'RemCTL doctor' header + context block first).

- detect_shell_name() -> str (remctl:6961): Path(os.environ.get('SHELL','')).name, or 'zsh' if SHELL empty.

CI-TESTABLE (pure given injected state): The whole check-gathering and result assembly is deterministic once you control: STORE_DIR existence/readability (env REMCTL_STORE_DIR + temp dirs with chmod), presence/absence of Data-*.sqlite files, CONFIG_DIR existence (REMCTL_CONFIG_DIR), the resolved exe path, the SHELL env (detect_shell_name), and the completion target file existence. platform/python checks are testable but platform is fixed to darwin in this env. The status/detail/fix tuples, the result dict shape, fail_count→exit-code mapping, the --json serialization (indent=2), the --for-agent agent_note injection, and print_check_report's formatting/summary pluralization are all pure functions of `checks` + flags — ideal for golden-output tests if gather_doctor_checks accepts injected dependencies (recommend refactoring it to take a struct of probes: storeAccessError, dbPath, eventKitStatus, reminderKitProbe, configDirExists, shell, completionExists). For Swift: model each check as data; test the gatherer with injected closures, and snapshot both JSON and human renderings.

ENVIRONMENT/GUI-DEPENDENT (NOT cleanly CI-testable): doctor_execution_context() (process_ancestry/ps walk, detect_terminal_app_name, mdfind in find_app_bundle) — depends on the live process tree, TERM_PROGRAM, and installed .app bundles; tests can at most assert shape/keys, not values. EventKit authorization status and RKPProbe() reflect the real TCC state and framework load of the running binary — environment-coupled (RKPProbe is deterministic-ish: returns 'reminderkit-ok' if REMStore class loads). full_disk_access_target_specs / find_app_bundle hit the filesystem and mdfind. None of doctor itself launches GUI or prompts TCC, so doctor remains runnable in CI without side effects (it just reports unknown/empty context).
findings.outwardFacing: doctor itself is READ-ONLY and side-effect-free for the user: it does NOT modify the system, does NOT launch any GUI, does NOT prompt TCC, does NOT write files. It only reads paths/env, shells out to `ps` (and `mdfind`/`open` ONLY transitively via full_disk_access_target_specs when building the database-fail fix text — find_app_bundle runs mdfind; full_disk_access_fix_text does NOT call open). Worst case it spawns `ps`/`mdfind` subprocesses for context. The genuinely outward-facing / hard-to-reverse behaviors live in the SIBLING commands (onboard launches the FDA helper + opens System Settings + can trigger TCC prompts; permissions launches the GUI helper / opens Settings / copies to clipboard; setup creates CONFIG_DIR and writes the completion script file). For Phase 4, doctor can ship as a safe in-process diagnostic; the GUI/TCC-prompting parts are isolated to onboard/permissions.
findings.implementationApproach:
ADAPT-TO-IN-PROCESS-REALITY (faithful where possible, re-framed for the three helper checks). Recommended Swift plan:

1) Model `DoctorCheck { name; status: .ok/.warn/.fail; detail: String; fix: String? }` and a `gatherDoctorChecks(probes:)` that takes injected probes (storeDir URL+readability, dbPath, configDir exists, shell, completion-target exists, eventKitAuthStatus, reminderKitProbe string, cliPath, exePath). This makes the gatherer fully CI-testable and mirrors gather_doctor_checks 1:1 for the portable checks.

2) PORT FAITHFULLY: platform (darwin always-ok in Swift; keep for parity — or rename detail to Swift/macOS version), store_dir (Paths.resolveStoreDir + FileManager.fileExists), database (REUSE Paths.storeAccessError + Paths.findMainDBPath — already byte-compatible; keep both branches incl. full_disk_access_fix_text equivalent), cli (CommandLine.arguments[0]/Bundle.main.executablePath + a `which remctl` lookup; preserve the quirk that status keys off existence while fix keys off PATH-presence), config_dir (Paths.resolveConfigDir), completion (port detect_shell_name + completion_target_path verbatim — these are filesystem-path conventions independent of runtime). 

3) RE-FRAME the python check: there is no Python interpreter. Either DROP it or replace with a runtime/OS check (e.g. macOS version >= min supported) so the slot is still informative; do NOT keep 'Install Python 3.10+' text.

4) RE-FRAME the three external-binary checks (bridge/private_helper/permissions_helper) — these are the CRITICAL changes:
   - `bridge` → rename to e.g. `eventkit` (or keep name 'bridge' for JSON-key parity but change semantics): probe in-process EventKit. Use EKEventStore().authorizationStatus(for: .reminder) (or .fullAccess on the new API). status: .ok when .authorized/.fullAccess; .warn (NOT fail, preserving Python's warn) when .notDetermined/.restricted/.denied; detail = human auth status; fix = 'Run remctl onboard to grant Reminders access.' Keep it WARN-not-FAIL to preserve exit-code parity.
   - `private_helper` → rename e.g. `reminderkit`: call RKPProbe() (ReminderKitPrivate.m:205 → 'reminderkit-ok'/'reminderkit-missing'). status .ok when 'reminderkit-ok' else .warn; detail = probe result; fix(on warn) = 'ReminderKit private framework unavailable; --private writes will fail.'
   - `permissions_helper` → DROP (no separate permissions binary in-process) OR fold into the database/FDA check. If kept for parity of the checks-array length, re-frame as a Full Disk Access status line derived from storeAccessError (ok when store readable, warn otherwise) — but that overlaps the database check, so dropping is cleaner. Document the divergence.

5) --json: emit indent=2 pretty JSON (NOT the space-free compact mode used for smart-list filter bytes) to match doctor; --for-agent: inject agent_note (JSON) / Agent-note line (human). Exit 1 iff any .fail.

6) doctor_execution_context: implement a best-effort Swift port (ProcessInfo + `ps` ancestry walk + TERM_PROGRAM/KNOWN_TERMINAL_APPS + codex special-case). It is environment-only; tests assert shape not values. The context block + agent note are important for the FDA-scoping UX, so keep them.

7) print_check_report: port the exact formatting ([LABEL] name: detail, 6-space dim fix lines, pluralized colored summary). doctor passes title=None and prints its own header/context first.

ArgumentParser: add @Flag --forAgent (name: .customLong("for-agent")) to Doctor alongside the existing JSONOptions. Do NOT use ArgumentParser's built-in completion generator here — that is for the `completion`/`setup` commands, a separate Phase-4 area; doctor only REPORTS whether the completion file exists.
risks: EXIT-CODE PARITY: the three helper checks are WARN (never FAIL) in Python, so they never affect exit code. If re-framed EventKit/ReminderKit checks are made FAIL, `remctl doctor` would start exiting 1 in environments where the old version exited 0 (e.g. EventKit not-yet-authorized). Keep them WARN to preserve exit-code behavior, or explicitly accept the divergence.

JSON-KEY PARITY: renaming check `name`s (bridge→eventkit, private_helper→reminderkit, dropping permissions_helper) changes the `checks[].name` values and the checks-array length in --json output. Any downstream/agent parser keyed on those names breaks. Decide whether to keep legacy names with new semantics (confusing) or rename (cleaner but a contract change) — and update the contract spec.
The `python` check has no in-process analog; silently dropping it shrinks the checks array and could surprise golden-output tests. Re-frame to an OS/runtime check or document removal.

doctor_execution_context relies on `ps` ancestry, TERM_PROGRAM, mdfind, and bundle lookups — flaky/empty in CI and sandboxes; the Swift port must degrade to effective_context='unknown' without erroring (matching Python's graceful fallbacks).

find_app_bundle runs `mdfind` and full_disk_access_target_specs/find_app_bundle are invoked transitively when building the database-FAIL fix text — so even read-only doctor can spawn mdfind and touch the filesystem; ensure timeouts/failures are swallowed (Python uses 5s timeouts and try/except).
The cli check's split logic (status from exists(), fix from PATH-presence) is subtle; a naive Swift port may set status and fix off the same predicate and diverge.

EventKit's authorizationStatus API changed (requestFullAccessToReminders / .fullAccess vs legacy .authorized) across macOS versions; the probe must map both to .ok or it will WARN spuriously on newer OSes. Note EventKitWriter.requestAccess() actively REQUESTS access (can trigger a TCC prompt) — doctor must use the non-prompting authorizationStatus(for:) query, NOT requestAccess(), to stay side-effect-free.

RKPProbe() only checks that REMStore class loads (NSClassFromString), not that ReminderKit operations will succeed — a 'reminderkit-ok' result does not guarantee private writes work; word the detail/fix carefully.

completion_target_path / detect_shell_name are pure path conventions and port cleanly, but the completion check only reports file existence; do not conflate with the separate `setup`/`completion` Phase-4 commands that actually generate scripts (ArgumentParser built-in generator).

findings.summary: cmd_onboard (remctl:7471) and cmd_permissions (remctl:7494) are the two outward-facing setup commands. Both center on the Full Disk Access (FDA) problem: EventKit grants live access, but direct SQLite reads of the Reminders store require FDA on the *running* binary, and macOS cannot grant FDA from the command line. The Python flow's job is to (a) trigger TCC prompts (EventKit + AppleScript Automation) and (b) help the user grant FDA by either launching a separate AppKit GUI helper (remctl-permissions.swift) or opening System Settings via the x-apple.systempreferences: URL scheme and printing guidance. onboard runs 4 checks (open_reminders/eventkit/automation/database), writes onboard-state.json, and — only in human mode, only if the database check mentions FDA — fires the helper/guidance. permissions full-disk-access launches the helper (or guidance) directly; in --json mode it is purely informational and launches nothing. The remctl-permissions.swift helper is a full standalone AppKit app (NSApplication.run) that opens a 600x560 window with draggable target rows, live 2-second status polling, opens System Settings on launch, copies a path to the clipboard, and can run a 'Run Doctor' subprocess via /bin/zsh -lc. KEY DECISION for the single-binary Swift port: the bridge/private helpers are already folded in-process (EventKitWriter calls requestFullAccessToReminders directly), so onboard's eventkit check should call that in-process instead of probing an external bridge binary. For the FDA *helper*, the recommended approach is to NOT port the AppKit GUI in-process (it would force the CLI to link AppKit + become an NSApplication, and the whole helper is convenience UI, not contract behavior). Instead: graceful-degrade to open System Settings via NSWorkspace + print the existing guidance text. permission_helper_available() then becomes effectively always-false (no external helper bundled), so both commands reliably take the guidance branch — which is the contract-defined, testable path.
keyFindings: FLOW (permissions full-disk-access): validate topic == 'full-disk-access' (else stderr 'Error: Unsupported permissions topic '<topic>'' + exit 1; argparse choices=['full-disk-access'] already blocks others with exit 2). Build targets = full_disk_access_target_specs(include_cli=True). If --json: print json.dumps({helper, available, targets}, indent=2) and RETURN (no GUI, no Settings opened). Else: try launch_full_disk_access_helper(include_cli=True, wait=a.wait); on success print_permission_helper_opened() and return; on failure print_full_disk_access_guidance(settings_opened=open_full_disk_access_settings(), rerun_command='remctl doctor'). Always exit 0 in human mode even if launch fails.

FLOW (onboard): result = run_onboarding(auto=False) -> gather_onboarding_checks() runs FOUR checks in fixed order [open_reminders, eventkit(bridge authorize), automation(osascript), database], computes ok/warnings/failures, ALWAYS writes <CONFIG_DIR>/onboard-state.json. If --json: print json.dumps(result, indent=2) — NO helper launch, NO Settings, NO clipboard side effects. Else (human): print 'RemCTL onboard' (bold) + dim approve-prompts line + blank + print_check_report(None, checks); then find the 'database' check and if needs_full_disk_access_guidance(db_check) (i.e. 'Full Disk Access' substring in its fix OR detail): try launch_full_disk_access_helper(include_cli=True) -> success: print_permission_helper_opened(); failure: print_full_disk_access_guidance(settings_opened=open_full_disk_access_settings(), rerun_command='remctl doctor'). Finally if result['failures']: sys.exit(1).

GUI/SYSTEM SIDE EFFECTS that fire: (1) onboard runs `open -a Reminders` then time.sleep(1) (launches Reminders.app GUI). (2) onboard's eventkit check shells the bridge with {action:'authorize'} which triggers the macOS Reminders TCC prompt. (3) onboard's automation check runs osascript -e 'tell application "Reminders" to get name of default list' which triggers the Automation (Apple Events) TCC prompt. (4) The FDA helper (remctl-permissions) is a separate GUI app: when launched it opens System Settings (NSWorkspace.open of x-apple.systempreferences URL), copies first target path to clipboard, shows a window, and polls every 2s. (5) Fallback open_full_disk_access_settings() runs `open <x-apple.systempreferences URL>` (opens System Settings to Full Disk Access pane). (6) print_full_disk_access_guidance copies the python path to clipboard via pbcopy. NO command itself programmatically grants TCC/FDA — macOS forbids that; everything is prompt-triggering or navigation.

remctl-permissions.swift IS a full AppKit GUI app (imports AppKit, ends with NSApplication.shared / app.run()). It parses --title/--subtitle/--target(title path subtitle, repeatable)/--after(title command, repeatable)/--no-open. On launch (applicationDidFinishLaunching): setActivationPolicy(.regular) [becomes a Dock app], opens System Settings (unless --no-open), copies first target path, builds a 600x560 NSWindow titled 'RemCTL Permissions' with header icon/title/subtitle, an 'Open Full Disk Access'/'Check Access'/'Done' button row, one draggable TargetRowView per --target (icon + title + subtitle + monospaced path + Copy Path/Reveal buttons + live status 'Checking...'/'✓ Access verified'(green)/'Needs access'(orange)), an output log NSTextView, and a button per --after command. Rows are NSDraggingSource (drag the binary's file URL into the Settings list). A Timer polls verifyPermissionTarget every 2.0s. verifyPermissionTarget: for python-like paths it spawns that interpreter with a glob/os.access probe of Data-*.sqlite (exit 0 = verified); otherwise checks remindersStoreReadable() directly. The 'Run Doctor' --after button runs `<cli> doctor` via /bin/zsh -lc with an augmented PATH and streams output to the log.

Default target fallback inside the helper itself: if NO --target passed, it injects one default target {title:'Current Python interpreter', path:'/usr/bin/python3', subtitle:'Fallback target for direct CLI reads.'}. This is a Python-era artifact and irrelevant once the CLI is a native Swift binary.

permission_helper_available() = current_permissions_path().exists() AND os.access(X_OK). current_permissions_path() honors REMCTL_PERMISSIONS_PATH env, else PERMISSIONS_PATH (sibling 'remctl-permissions' next to the script), else shutil.which('remctl-permissions'). In the single Swift binary with no bundled external helper, this is effectively always False (the testable, deterministic state).

Already-folded-in-process reality: EventKitWriter.swift:33 already calls store.requestFullAccessToReminders() in-process (the bridge 'authorize' action is gone). Paths.swift already mirrors the Python FDA logic: storeAccessError() reproduces the exact 'Direct CLI reads are blocked...' message (using Bundle.main.executablePath as the context id), and findMainDBPath() picks the largest Data-*.sqlite. So onboard's eventkit check and database check both have native in-process equivalents already in the codebase — no external helper needed for them.

Topic validation: only 'full-disk-access' is accepted. ArgumentParser equivalent should restrict the positional to that one value. Python keeps a manual `if a.topic != 'full-disk-access'` guard (stderr 'Error: Unsupported permissions topic '<topic>'' + exit 1) that is technically unreachable behind argparse choices but the contract (spec line 1117) says it must be preserved. In Swift, an enum-typed @Argument gives exit 64 (ArgumentParser validation) for bad values; to match Python's exit-1 + exact message you'd take a raw String argument and guard manually.

Paths.storeAccessError/findMainDBPath are already covered by existing Swift tests.\n\nENVIRONMENT/GUI-DEPENDENT (NOT CI-testable, must gate behind seams or live-only): `open -a Reminders` + sleep(1); the EventKit requestFullAccessToReminders() TCC prompt; the osascript Automation TCC prompt; NSWorkspace/`open` of x-apple.systempreferences URLs (opens System Settings); pbcopy clipboard write; launching the AppKit helper window; the helper's 2s polling, drag-and-drop, Reveal-in-Finder, and 'Run Doctor' zsh subprocess. mdfind/ps ancestry probing is slow + machine-specific. None of these should run in CI; tests should assert the decision (which branch is taken / which strings print) with side effects injected as no-op closures.
findings.outwardFacing: HIGHLY outward-facing — these are the most system-modifying commands in the whole CLI. Specifically: (1) onboard launches Reminders.app GUI (`open -a Reminders`). (2) onboard triggers TWO TCC prompts the user must click through: Reminders access (EventKit) and Automation/Apple Events (osascript) — these create persistent TCC.db grants. (3) Both commands open System Settings to the Full Disk Access pane (navigation, not a grant). (4) Both can spawn a separate full GUI app (remctl-permissions) that takes over the Dock, opens a window, and itself opens System Settings + writes the clipboard. (5) The helper's 'Run Doctor' button executes an arbitrary shell command (`<cli> doctor` here) via /bin/zsh -lc. (6) Clipboard is overwritten (pbcopy / NSPasteboard). (7) onboard ALWAYS writes <CONFIG_DIR>/onboard-state.json (creating CONFIG_DIR) — this is the gate that suppresses first-launch auto-onboarding, so writing it has lasting behavioral effect. HARD-TO-REVERSE / user-visible: the TCC grants (require manual revocation in System Settings), the onboard-state.json file, the clipboard contents, and any Dock/GUI takeover by the helper. NONE of these can be exercised safely in CI or non-interactively. NOTE: no command can programmatically grant FDA/TCC — macOS prohibits it; all 'writes' are prompt-triggers, navigation, a state file, and clipboard.
findings.implementationApproach:
RECOMMENDED: ADAPT to in-process reality + GRACEFUL-DEGRADE the GUI helper (do NOT port remctl-permissions.swift's AppKit window in-process). Concretely:

(A) permission_helper_available() -> hardcode to a single source of truth that is FALSE in the shipped single binary (no external 'remctl-permissions' is bundled). Honor REMCTL_PERMISSIONS_PATH only if you want to keep an escape hatch; otherwise always-false is cleaner and makes both commands deterministically take the guidance branch. permissions --json must still emit {helper: <path or empty/derived>, available: false, targets: [...]} — keep the key order + indent=2; just rename 'Current Python interpreter' target to the remctl binary's own path (since there's no separate python interpreter) with an equivalent subtitle.

(B) launch_full_disk_access_helper -> since the helper isn't bundled, this returns false and the code falls through to print_full_disk_access_guidance(settings_opened: openFullDiskAccessSettings()). Implement openFullDiskAccessSettings() via NSWorkspace.shared.open(URL) over the two x-apple.systempreferences URLs, OR shell `open <url>` to avoid linking AppKit. Recommendation: shell `open` (Process /usr/bin/open) to keep the CLI AppKit-free and match Python's exact mechanism; it returns rc you can map to settings_opened. Guard all of this behind an injected side-effect seam so tests pass settings_opened/copied as fixed bools.

(C) onboard's eventkit check -> call the EXISTING in-process EventKitWriter.authorize() (EventKitWriter.swift) instead of a bridge subprocess; reframe the ok detail to reference the remctl binary (not a bridge path) and produce calendarCount/defaultList from store.calendars(for:.reminder)/defaultCalendarForNewReminders. The 'helper unavailable' warn variants no longer apply (drop them or keep only the fail-on-not-granted path). This is a CONTRACT REFRAME the spec already anticipates ('bridge availability checks must be RE-FRAMED for in-process reality').

(D) onboard's database check -> reuse Paths.storeAccessError()/findMainDBPath() (already present) + full_disk_access_fix_text equivalent. open_reminders (`open -a Reminders` + 0.5-1s) and automation (osascript) probes port directly via Process, but MUST be injectable closures so the command core is testable without side effects.

(E) topic validation -> take the positional as a raw String and manually guard `topic != 'full-disk-access'` -> stderr exact message + exit 1, to match Python (an enum @Argument would give the wrong exit code/message). Optionally also register the value for completion.

(F) Structure each command as a pure core (returns stdout/stderr/exit + a list of 'effects' or takes injected effect closures) + a thin run() that performs real effects — mirroring how Import/Add are already split (perform vs run) in OpsCommands.swift. This keeps the JSON shapes, guidance text, and branch logic fully CI-testable while quarantining the GUI/TCC/clipboard/`open` side effects to the live run path.

Do NOT fold AppKit in-process: it forces the whole CLI to become an NSApplication (.regular activation, app.run()), pulls in AppKit, and replaces nothing contract-required — the window is pure convenience. The 'open Settings + printed guidance' path is the contract-defined fallback and is what every CI/headless/agent context will hit anyway.
risks: TCC prompts are one-shot per binary identity and persist in TCC.db. A native Swift remctl has a DIFFERENT code identity than the Python interpreter, so onboard's EventKit/Automation grants must be re-approved for the Swift binary; previously-granted Python grants do NOT carry over. The 'context' identity (Bundle.main.executablePath) shifts from a python path to the remctl binary path — this changes target paths AND guidance text. Ensure the contract reframe documents that the FDA target is now the remctl binary, not /usr/bin/python3.

If permission_helper_available() is hardcoded false, permissions --json 'available' flips to false vs the Python contract value (which depended on the sibling helper existing). This is an intentional, documented divergence for the single-binary reality — but get sign-off so parity tests are updated, not treated as regressions. The 'helper' key value also needs a sensible value (empty string, the binary path, or a derived path).

The AppKit helper is genuinely unportable into the same process without making the CLI an NSApplication; any attempt to 'fold it in' risks breaking headless/CI/agent invocation (app.run() blocks, .regular activation policy, AppKit link). Strongly avoid.

Side effects (open -a Reminders + sleep, osascript, `open <settings-url>`, pbcopy/NSPasteboard, onboard-state.json write) will fire on any real invocation — they MUST be behind injected seams or the command's tests will mutate the developer's machine (clipboard, launch Reminders, write state file that then suppresses auto-onboard). The existing Import/Add perform-vs-run split is the pattern to follow.

ArgumentParser exit codes differ from argparse: a malformed/missing positional gives ArgumentParser exit 64, not Python's argparse exit 2; and an enum-typed topic would never reach the manual exit-1 guard. To preserve the exact 'Error: Unsupported permissions topic ...' + exit 1 behavior the positional must be a raw String validated by hand.

onboard --json vs human divergence is load-bearing: JSON mode must NOT launch the helper, open Settings, or touch the clipboard (only run_onboarding + state write). It's easy to accidentally run the side effects unconditionally; gate them strictly on the human branch AND on needs_full_disk_access_guidance(db_check).

full_disk_access_targets() (the string-list variant used by guidance) synthesizes an extra 'recommended for CLI use' terminal line when no .app target exists, and is DISTINCT from full_disk_access_target_specs() (the dict list used by --json/helper). The two must not be conflated — guidance text and JSON targets are built by different functions with different shapes.

onboard's two embedded rerun commands differ by design: the database check's fix text uses 'remctl doctor --for-agent' while the printed guidance uses 'remctl doctor'. Preserve both exact strings; do not unify them.

findings.area: list-symbols --preview/--html (RemindersUICore native badge asset rendering → HTML contact sheet)
findings.summary: cmd_list_symbols (remctl:5044) has three branches. The non-HTML JSON/plain branches are ALREADY ported in Swift (Sources/RemindersControl/Commands/ListCommands.swift:589-614); the only NotImplemented piece is the --html/--preview branch (remctl:5046-5058). That branch builds a standalone, self-contained HTML "contact sheet" of all 73 official list badges, writes it to a file (default CONFIG_DIR/list-symbols.html, or --html PATH), prints `HTML preview: {path}` to stdout, and — only with --preview — also runs `open <path>` to launch it in the browser. The native badge images are extracted by compiling+running an INLINE Swift program (`swift -` reading source on stdin) that loads /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/RemindersUICore.framework as an NSBundle, calls `bundle.image(forResource: <asset>)` for each of the 73 `ListBadge*` asset names, converts each NSImage→TIFF→NSBitmapImageRep→PNG, writes PNGs to a tempdir; Python then base64-encodes each PNG and embeds it as `data:image/png;base64,...` in the HTML, rendered white via CSS `filter: brightness(0) invert(1)` on an orange circular badge. KEY: the Swift port's RemindersControl target ALREADY links AppKit, so this Swift-subprocess-on-Swift dance can be done IN-PROCESS — no `swift` toolchain needed at runtime. RemindersUICore is a private framework loaded by path via NSBundle at runtime (not link-time), so it works regardless of build linkage.
keyFindings: BRANCH TRIGGER (remctl:5046): `if getattr(a,'html',None) is not None or getattr(a,'preview',False)`. --html uses argparse nargs='?' const='' — so bare `--html` => '' (still triggers; the `is not None` test is on presence not truthiness), `--html PATH` => PATH. --json+--html/--preview => stderr `Error: --json cannot be combined with --html or --preview.` exit 1 (this guard is ALREADY ported in Swift ListCommands.swift:582-585, before the NotImplemented throw).

WRITE+OPEN (remctl:5051-5057): calls write_list_symbols_html(a.html or None) ('' maps to None => default path), on RuntimeError prints `Error: {e}` exit 1, then `if a.preview: subprocess.run(['open', str(output_path)], check=False)` (return code ignored), then ALWAYS prints `HTML preview: {output_path}` to stdout. --preview both WRITES the file AND opens it; --html only writes.

DEFAULT PATH (remctl:4744-4745): default_list_symbols_html_path() = CONFIG_DIR / 'list-symbols.html'. CONFIG_DIR (remctl:54) = resolve_config_dir('remctl'). Swift equivalent exists: Paths.resolveConfigDir(appName:'remctl') in Sources/RemindersControl/Runtime/Paths.swift:24 (REMCTL_CONFIG_DIR > XDG_CONFIG_HOME/remctl > ~/.config/remctl). write_list_symbols_html does output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) then write_text(html, encoding='utf-8'); a.html path is .expanduser()'d (remctl:5037).

ASSET EXPORT (remctl:4747-4801, export_list_symbol_asset_data): (1) finds `swift` via shutil.which or /usr/bin/swift — RuntimeError `Swift is required to export Reminders badge assets for the HTML preview.` if missing; (2) checks REMINDERS_UI_CORE_BUNDLE (remctl:4736 = /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/RemindersUICore.framework) exists — RuntimeError `RemindersUICore framework not found at {path}.` if missing; (3) runs the inline Swift program via `swift - <bundle> <tmpdir> <asset>...` feeding the source on stdin, capture_output, text. Non-zero exit => RuntimeError(stderr or stdout or 'asset export failed', stripped). Then reads each `{asset}.png` from tmpdir and base64-encodes it into a dict keyed by asset name.

INLINE SWIFT PROGRAM (remctl:4754-4785): imports AppKit+Foundation; args = bundle-path, output-dir, then asset names. `Bundle(path:)` (exit 65 if nil), createDirectory(withIntermediateDirectories:true). Per asset: `bundle.image(forResource: asset)` -> `.tiffRepresentation` -> `NSBitmapImageRep(data:)` -> `.representation(using:.png, properties:[:])` -> write to `{asset}.png`; assets that fail any step append to `missing`. If any missing: stderr `Missing badge assets: <comma-joined>` exit 66. Usage error exit 64, bad-bundle exit 65.

HTML FALLBACK PER-CARD (remctl:4822-4826): for each row, if base64 PNG present => ``; ELSE => `{preview}` (the Unicode glyph). NOTE this per-card fallback only fires for individually-missing assets; if the WHOLE export raises RuntimeError (swift/framework missing), the command aborts with exit 1 and writes NO file. The contract (line 641) explicitly says the Swift port should keep asset rendering OPTIONAL and fall back to the preview glyph per-card when a PNG is missing.

SWATCHES (remctl:4805-4817): build_list_symbols_html calls list_color_preview_rows() (remctl:340) over LIST_COLOR_MAP (remctl:214, 10 colors red/orange/yellow/green/blue/purple/brown/gray/cyan/teal IN THAT ORDER). Each color row = {name, hex (rgb_to_hex '#{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}'), highlight (blend_rgb toward white amount=0.34, rounded)}. The 2nd swatch (index 1 = orange) starts active/aria-pressed=true and seeds --badge/--badge-highlight via inline JS click handlers.

Swift Package ALREADY links AppKit on RemindersControl (Package.swift:43 .linkedFramework('AppKit')) and the ReminderKitPrivate Obj-C target uses `-F /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks`. ReminderKitPrivate.m:1290 already constructs NSImage. So NSImage/NSBitmapImageRep PNG conversion can run IN-PROCESS in Swift — the entire `swift -` subprocess is unnecessary; only NSBundle(path:)+bundle.image(forResource:) against RemindersUICore is needed at runtime.

With --preview additionally spawns `/usr/bin/open {path}` (failure ignored, no extra output). findings.ciTestability:
PURE / CI-testable: build_list_symbols_html is a deterministic pure function of (rows, image_data dict). The HTML string structure, escaping, swatch generation (LIST_COLOR_MAP order, rgb_to_hex, blend_rgb amount=0.34), the per-card img-vs-fallback selection, the `HTML preview: {path}` stdout line, the --json mutual-exclusion guard, CONFIG_DIR path resolution, and the `--html ''→default` mapping are ALL testable without any framework/GUI by injecting a fake image_data map (incl. empty map => all-fallback path) and an injectable `open` launcher (the WriteCommands.Open pattern already proves the seam). The 73-symbol table and 10-color swatch data are already CI-covered constants.

ENVIRONMENT/GUI-dependent (NOT CI-verifiable): the actual native PNG extraction (requires the RemindersUICore private framework present + readable AND the asset names still valid on the host macOS version), and the `open` browser launch. These should sit behind an injected boundary so tests exercise the fallback (empty image_data) and success (stub image_data) paths deterministically. The contract's reminders-tests reference list (line 2539-2542) only asserts on the PLAIN/JSON output, not the HTML branch — so there is no parity test fixture forcing byte-exact HTML.
findings.outwardFacing: YES, outward-facing on three axes: (1) WRITES A FILE to disk — default ~/.config/remctl/list-symbols.html (or arbitrary --html PATH, with parent dirs created); (2) LAUNCHES A GUI — with --preview runs `open` which opens the user's default browser; (3) LOADS A PRIVATE FRAMEWORK at runtime (RemindersUICore via NSBundle) and reads bundled image assets. Hard-to-reverse: minimal — it only creates one HTML file (overwrites if exists) and opens a browser tab; no Reminders data is mutated, no TCC/permission prompt (NSBundle asset reads from a system framework don't trigger TCC; no EventKit access). The Python version additionally shells out to the `swift` compiler at runtime (compiles+runs an inline program in a tempdir) — that toolchain dependency is the most fragile/outward part and is the prime candidate for removal in Swift.
findings.implementationApproach:
RECOMMEND: ADAPT-TO-IN-PROCESS + GRACEFUL-DEGRADE (not faithful subprocess port). Rationale: the RemindersControl target already links AppKit (Package.swift:43) and ReminderKitPrivate already uses `-F /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks`, so the native PNG export can run IN-PROCESS in Swift via `Bundle(path: REMINDERS_UI_CORE_BUNDLE)` + `bundle.image(forResource:)` + `NSBitmapImageRep`/`representation(using:.png)` — eliminating the entire `swift -` compile-and-run subprocess (which is slow, requires the Xcode/Swift toolchain at runtime, and is the most failure-prone path). This drops the `Swift is required...` RuntimeError entirely. CONCRETE PLAN: 1) Port build_list_symbols_html VERBATIM as a pure Swift function `func buildListSymbolsHTML(rows:, imageDataByAsset: [String:String]) -> String` — keep the exact HTML/CSS/JS bytes, html-escape every interpolation (use a small escaper matching Python html.escape: & < > and quotes), reuse officialListSymbols + a Swift listColorPreviewRows() over a LIST_COLOR_MAP (10 colors, exact order) with rgbToHex (uppercase %02X) and blendRgb(amount:0.34, rounded). Decide whether to keep the literal `--private` in the embedded hint

— the plain-text output already drops --private (ListCommands.swift:607 documents that deviation); be consistent: I'd KEEP the in-HTML hint as a static string and DROP --private to match the rest of the Swift port (document it). 2) Asset export as `func exportListSymbolAssetData(rows:) throws -> [String:String]` using AppKit in-process: if RemindersUICore bundle missing OR Bundle load fails => throw the `RemindersUICore framework not found...` error (faithful). For PER-ASSET misses, do NOT throw — collect into the dict only the successful ones, leaving missing assets absent so buildHTML renders the `.fallback` glyph (this realizes the contract's 'keep rendering optional, per-card glyph fallback' guidance, line 641). OPTIONAL: a `--strict`/env to restore the all-or-nothing `Missing badge assets:` behavior, but default to degrade. 3) Wire write+open: resolve path (Paths.resolveConfigDir + 'list-symbols.html' default; expand tilde for --html), `FileManager.createDirectory(withIntermediateDirectories:true)` on parent, write UTF-8, print `HTML preview: {path}`. For --preview reuse the existing `/usr/bin/open` launcher seam (WriteCommands.Open.launchWithOpen) injected for testability. 4) Keep the existing --json guard (already in place). DO NOT use ArgumentParser's built-in completion generator here (that's the separate `completion` command); irrelevant to this command. 5) DECISION on whole-framework-missing: faithfully keep exit-1 with `Error: RemindersUICore framework not found at ...` — but since per-asset degrade now means a present-but-incomplete framework still produces a full glyph-fallback sheet, the only hard failure left is the framework being entirely absent. ALTERNATIVE worth offering the planner: degrade even THAT to a glyph-only sheet (pass empty imageData, still write+print path, maybe a stderr note) so the command never fails on machines lacking the private framework — this is the most robust and best matches 'keep asset rendering optional'. I lean toward: framework-missing => still emit the glyph-only HTML (warn on stderr), making --html/--preview always succeed; this is a deliberate, documented deviation from the Python exit-1.
risks: Asset names may drift across macOS versions: the 73 `ListBadge*` IDs are hardcoded; if RemindersUICore renames/removes assets, `bundle.image(forResource:)` returns nil for those. Faithful Python would abort with `Missing badge assets:`; the recommended per-card degrade silently shows glyphs instead — better UX but a parity deviation. Flag this choice to the planner.

RemindersUICore is a PRIVATE framework; the path /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/RemindersUICore.framework may not exist on all macOS versions or may move. NSBundle(path:) load can fail even when the dir exists. CI/sandbox machines almost certainly cannot load it — so the success path is UNVERIFIABLE in CI; only the glyph-fallback/empty-imageData path is testable.

Whole-command failure semantics: if the planner wants byte-faithful Python parity, the framework-missing case must keep exit-1 + the exact error string. The recommended graceful-degrade (always succeed with glyph-only sheet) changes the exit code and adds stderr output — must be an explicit, documented decision.

html.escape parity: Python's html_lib.escape(s) escapes & < > and (by default quote=True) " and '. The Swift escaper must match (esp. the & ordering and quote handling) or the emitted HTML bytes differ from Python; matters only if anyone diff-tests the HTML (no contract fixture currently does).

The embedded hint

still literally contains `--private`; the rest of the Swift port removed --private. Keeping it verbatim contradicts the plain-text deviation (ListCommands.swift:607). Pick one and document — recommend dropping --private in the HTML hint too for internal consistency.

blend_rgb uses Python round() (banker's rounding) at amount=0.34; Swift `.rounded()` is round-half-away-from-zero. For these specific 10 colors verify the highlight hex matches, or replicate banker's rounding, else swatch --badge-highlight values differ by 1 in a channel.
Dropping the `swift` subprocess removes the `Swift is required...` RuntimeError path entirely — that error string becomes dead/untestable. Fine, but note it so no test asserts on it.

decisionsForUser.header: completion: verbatim hand-written literals vs ArgumentParser built-in generator
decisionsForUser.question: Port the 3 hand-written shell scripts byte-for-byte, or switch to ArgumentParser's --generate-completion-script?
decisionsForUser.recommendation: VERBATIM. The contract pins script structure (spec lines 1037-1040: 47 zsh / 45 bash command counts, exact start/end markers); AP's generator emits different text/paths and breaks byte-parity golden tests. Verbatim also keeps the 3 install target paths correct and ships the same scripts regardless of how Swift parses args. Cost is double-maintenance of the literals (same burden Python already carries - acceptable for a faithful port). Optional future: expose AP's generator as an UNDOCUMENTED extra, but keep `completion <shell>` verbatim as the contract surface. Note this requires faithfully reproducing the cross-shell inconsistencies (bash/fish carry --date-today-include-past-due, zsh omits) - do not 'fix' them.

decisionsForUser.header: GUI / permissions approach: fold AppKit in-process vs graceful-degrade
decisionsForUser.question: Port remctl-permissions.swift's AppKit GUI window into the single binary, or graceful-degrade to open System Settings + print guidance?
decisionsForUser.recommendation: GRACEFUL-DEGRADE. Folding AppKit in-process forces the whole CLI to become an NSApplication (.regular activation, app.run() blocks) and link AppKit for a window that is pure convenience, not contract behavior - and would break headless/CI/agent invocation. Instead hardcode permissionHelperAvailable()=false so both onboard and permissions deterministically take the guidance branch (open Settings via /usr/bin/open + printed guidance), which is the contract-defined fallback every headless context hits anyway. CONSEQUENCE needing sign-off: permissions --json 'available' flips from Python's value (which depended on a sibling helper existing) to false, and the 'helper' key needs a sensible value (recommend the remctl binary path or empty string). Also reframe onboard's eventkit check to the already-in-process EventKitWriter.authorize() (EventKitWriter.swift:22) rather than a bridge subprocess - the codebase already did this fold.

decisionsForUser.header: list-symbols --html: faithful exit-1 on missing framework vs always-degrade
decisionsForUser.question: When RemindersUICore is entirely absent, keep Python's hard exit-1 `Error: RemindersUICore framework not found...`, or degrade to a glyph-only HTML sheet?
decisionsForUser.recommendation: DEGRADE to glyph-only (always succeed, write the file with empty imageData, optional stderr note). Per-asset misses already degrade to the .fallback glyph per the contract's 'keep asset rendering optional' (line 641), so the only remaining hard failure is the framework being entirely absent - and degrading even that makes the command robust on every machine (CI, sandbox, future macOS where the private framework moved). This is a DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED deviation from Python's exit-1 (changes exit code + adds stderr). It also drops the `swift -` subprocess entirely (AppKit already linked, Package.swift:43), removing the runtime toolchain dependency AND the now-dead `Swift is required...` error string. If strict parity is mandated instead, keep exit-1 for framework-missing and gate behind a --strict/env flag for the all-or-nothing per-asset behavior.

decisionsForUser.header: doctor: re-frame check names/length vs preserve Python's
decisionsForUser.question: The python/bridge/private_helper/permissions_helper checks have no faithful in-process analog. Rename them (bridge->eventkit, private_helper->reminderkit, drop permissions_helper, reframe/drop python) or keep legacy names with new semantics?
decisionsForUser.recommendation: RE-FRAME with new names + DROP permissions_helper, and keep all re-framed checks WARN (never FAIL) to preserve exit-code parity (Python's helper checks were WARN, so only platform/store_dir/database/cli failures cause exit 1 - keep it that way). This changes checks[].name values and the checks-array length in --json, which is a CONTRACT CHANGE any agent parser keyed on those names will see - update the contract spec accordingly. Alternative (keep legacy names, new semantics) is more confusing and was explicitly flagged as such. For the python check specifically: replace with a macOS-version/runtime check (keep the slot informative) rather than silently dropping it (which would surprise golden tests). Must use non-prompting authorizationStatus(for:) NOT requestAccess() so doctor stays side-effect-free.

If behavior is ported without fixing these structs, `remctl completion bash`, `remctl setup --shell zsh --doctor`, `remctl permissions full-disk-access` fail to parse. Fix signatures FIRST.

BYTE-PARITY HAZARD: completion literals must be copied EXACTLY including the trailing newline inside each triple-quoted constant and the deliberate cross-shell inconsistencies; a 'helpful' dev normalizing them breaks the pinned contract (spec 1037-1040). ~540 lines of fragile copy.

Build the shared helpers + doctor checks core first.

EXIT-CODE PARITY: re-framed EventKit/ReminderKit checks must stay WARN; making them FAIL would make doctor exit 1 in environments where Python exited 0 (e.g. EventKit not-yet-authorized). EventKit auth API differs by OS - map BOTH .fullAccess and legacy .authorized to .ok or it WARNs spuriously on newer macOS.

TCC IDENTITY SHIFT: the native Swift binary has a different code identity than the Python interpreter, so onboard's EventKit/Automation grants must be re-approved; the FDA target/guidance now points at the remctl binary, not /usr/bin/python3. Contract reframe must document this; permissions --json 'available' flips to false (needs sign-off so parity tests are updated, not treated as regressions).

SIDE-EFFECT LEAKAGE in tests: onboard/permissions side effects (open -a Reminders + sleep, osascript, open Settings, pbcopy, onboard-state.json write that then SUPPRESSES future auto-onboard) will mutate the dev machine unless strictly behind injected seams gated on the human branch AND needsFullDiskAccessGuidance. JSON mode must launch nothing. Follow the existing Import/Add perform-vs-run split.

PRIVATE-FRAMEWORK UNVERIFIABILITY: RemindersUICore success path and RKPProbe framework-load are not testable in CI/sandbox; only fallback/glyph paths are. Asset names (73 ListBadge* IDs) may drift across macOS versions - the recommended per-card degrade silently shows glyphs (UX win, parity deviation).

SUBTLE LOGIC TRAPS: doctor cli check splits status (from exists()) vs fix (from PATH-presence) - a naive same-predicate port diverges. fullDiskAccessTargetSpecs (dict, for JSON) vs fullDiskAccessTargets (string list, for guidance, synthesizes extra terminal line) are DISTINCT shapes - do not conflate. onboard's two rerun strings differ by design ('remctl doctor --for-agent' in db-check fix vs 'remctl doctor' in guidance) - preserve both. blendRgb rounding (Python banker's vs Swift round-half-away) may shift the 10 swatch highlight hexes by 1 channel.
